newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Bongaigaon refinery restarts after shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Indian Bongaigaon refinery restarts after shutdown.

text.p: India's Bongaigaon refinery has restarted full operations on Wednesday after crude throughput was halted last Thursday following a pipeline burst, said J.M.B. Baruah, chairman and managing director of Bongaigaon refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd.
He said crude throughput was an equivalent rate of 1.2 million tonnes per year, compared with normal crude throughput of 1.6 million tonnes per year.
Baruah said the refinery started to circulate crude on Monday and received products as of Wednesday.
The refinery has two crude distillation units (CDUs), each with a production capacity of 1.35 million tonnes per year.

At the time of the burst one CDU was already shut down for operational reasons. The other CDU was shut down following the pipeline burst. But supplies of oil products from the refinery, which includes four upgrading units and a petrochemical plant, were not disrupted due to adequate stocks.

Two Indian oil refineries were closed last week after the pipeline burst. The refineries, at Bongaigaon in the northeastern state of Assam and Barauni in the neighbouring state of Bihar, were shut down after crude spurting from the burst pipeline caught fire and burned for seven hours last Thursday.
The pipeline burst at Hajo, 30 km (19 miles) west of Assam's capital, Guwahati.
